visualReview.notes: Personally inspected all seven current portable and seven shared views. Eight estimated cells, the meeting hall and common room form a modest terraced courtyard complex. Each has a complete roof, real open doorway and closed backing walls. Earth, plaster and timber bindings work; near views show lintels and beam ends. Four flat roof silhouettes and estimated parapets are coherent. Missing original room census, plan and sections are openly estimated.

mediumFiReview.notes: Personally inspected all23 current context frames, four authored levels and transitions, plus original unmasked field. Every level retains the ten whole roofed rooms and doors; distant level omits thin parapets and timber. Original steep terrain can hide much of the annex from uphill/default south views, while opposite/detail views show the ensemble. Some uphill lower walls intersect the coarse source slope and downhill plinths are exposed. Terrain remains unchanged; historical benches and exact ground ties are unknown. Modest final1.2m plinths replace the oversized initial corner-envelope foundations before acceptance.

limitations: Estimated historical monastic cells, meeting hall and common rooms adjoining the distinct sanctuary. Written room functions are archaeological facts; dimensions, eight-cell census, sections and south-side layout are original reconstruction estimates.

DAFA written excavation description confirms sanctuary plus cells, meeting hall and common rooms. Eight cells, their arrangement around a small court, all widths/heights/roof profiles, doors, materials and precise700CEcondition are original estimates; no excavation plan, photo or artwork supplied geometry. This is a plausible structural interpretation, not an archaeological survey.

The annex centre is estimated22m south of the unchanged sanctuary point. Modern coarse terrain precedes sections; modest1.2m plinths support centre-grade floor estimates, rather than tall corner-envelope foundations. Uphill walls can intersect coarse ground and downhill plinths can be exposed. Historical benches and vertical ties are unknown; the source field is unchanged without flattening or masking.

Four levels retain all ten estimated rooms, actual door openings, flat roofs and terraced plinths; district and closer levels retain parapets. Near levels add timber beam ends, lintels and slight roof lips. Plain adobe, lime plaster, rammed earth and timber are original material interpretations. No decoration or artifact replicas.
